title: Count Stable Subarrays
summary: Given an integer array nums, for each query [li, ri] in a 2D array queries, calculate the count of stable subarrays within nums[li..ri].
statement: Given an integer array nums, for each query [li, ri] in a 2D array queries, calculate the count of stable subarrays within nums[li..ri]. A subarray is stable if no element is greater than any preceding element. Return an array ans where ans[i] is the count of stable subarrays for the i-th query. A single-element subarray is considered stable.
constraints: nums and queries each contain up to 100,000 entries.
A stable subarray is contiguous and nondecreasing; single elements qualify.
For each inclusive query range, count stable subarrays lying wholly inside it.
hints: Split nums into maximal nondecreasing runs; every stable subarray lies inside exactly one run.
Prefix-sum each full run’s triangular subarray count and store its start.
For a query, binary-search the first and last touched runs, add full interior runs, and use triangular counts for clipped edge pieces.
The run partition is disjoint and exhaustive, so these pieces count every contained stable subarray once.
editorial: The run partition is disjoint and exhaustive, so these pieces count every contained stable subarray once.

tests.explanation: The three ranges contain two, three, and four nondecreasing subarrays.
Equal values form one length-two stable subarray, giving counts three and one.
